candidates.current_role: Denton County Judge since 2019
candidates.background: Andy Eads is a fifth-generation Denton County resident who served on the Denton County Commissioners Court before becoming county judge in 2019. He holds a bachelor's degree in business administration from Howard Payne University and a master's in public administration from the University of North Texas. He lives in Flower Mound.

priorities.text: Campaigns on keeping property taxes low, strengthening public safety, improving transportation infrastructure, and promoting economic development.
Says managing rapid growth in a county of more than one million residents is the county's biggest challenge.
Says he will plan ahead and work with cities, regional partners and state leaders, and keep county government from growing faster than needed.
Says he wants to keep property taxes low through the senior tax freeze and homestead exemption.

promises.text: Says he will partner with the Texas Department of Transportation on state highway, farm-to-market road and interstate projects in the county.

record.text: Championed two countywide road bond elections and credits himself with work on SH 114, US 380 reconstruction, the I-635 agreement and the 35Express project.

The FY2027 recommended county budget presented to the Commissioners Court in August 2026 was about $494.5 million with a tax rate of $0.183394 per $100, described by the budget office as the lowest since at least 1986 and a 1.4% decrease from FY2026.
The FY2027 recommended budget keeps a homestead exemption (1% of value, minimum $5,000) for a seventh year and the senior and disabled homestead tax ceiling for an eighth year.

notes.text: Faces Democrat Nick Pappas in the November 3, 2026 general election.

q_county_tax.summary: Lists keeping property taxes low and disciplined spending among his top priorities, while also prioritizing road investment.

issue_notes.summary: Emphasizes partnerships with TxDOT and regional agencies on highway and road projects.
